P63/mmc hcp substitutional model: Fe0.84Si0.16 on 2c. Source identifies the hcp topology but does not refine chemical site occupancies; these enforce the measured bulk composition. Reference axes derive from 2014 Table S1 row 19 at 59.3958006581 GPa and 1186.915 K, not ambient conditions. The fixed structural c/a is a diffraction reference, not an EOS prediction of anisotropic compression.

## Observation datasets

### fischer\_2014\_table\_s1\_pvt

- **Description:** All 211 source observations, including excluded phases and pressure-marker observations; derived cell volumes supplement unchanged numeric source inputs.
- **Kind:** pressure\_volume\_temperature\_multiphase\_with\_calibrant
- **Reference:**
    - **Authors:** Fischer; Campbell; Caracas; Reaman; Heinz; Dera; Prakapenka
    - **Year:** 2014
    - **Title:** Equations of state in the Fe–FeSi system at high pressures and temperatures
    - **Source:** Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth
    - **Volume:** 119
    - **Locator:** 2810-2827
    - **DOI:** 10.1002/2013JB010898
- **Source location:** 2014 official Table S1, source worksheet row numbers retained
- **Associated EOS records:** fe084si016\_hcp\_fischer\_2014\_bm3\_1; fe084si016\_hcp\_fischer\_2014\_vinet\_2
- **Notes:** Original numerical precision is retained. Source zero uncertainties remain zero, blank uncertainties remain blank. No open data license was identified. The CSV contains factual measurements, not the source table image or layout. Sample temperatures already include the source gradient correction and must not be corrected again. Asterisks are recorded in source\_flags and their numeric fields left blank: \* means one d-spacing, uncertainty undefined; \*\* in Table S2 means phase detected but no reliable lattice parameter. The exceptional S2 row 62 marks both phase columns \*\*, which is preserved without repair. Derived cubic volumes are a^3; hcp volumes are sqrt(3)/2\*a^3\*(c/a). Covariance of a and c/a is not given, so no independent-error volume sigma is fabricated. The complete S2 data also support the withheld B2 audit. KBr lattice uncertainties are standard errors across indexed d-spacings; pressure errors propagate marker lattice and temperature uncertainty. The 2012 source also identifies sample lattice errors as standard errors. The 2014 temperature errors combine 100 K analytical uncertainty, differences between the two sample sides and thickness correction; no confidence level is specified.
